review_notes: I read the whole file with attention to its simp interface: the three scoped simp lemmas on ValuationSubring (lines 112, 191, 1129), coords_zero and coords_some, the `attribute [-simp]` header, and every simp/simpa call. I checked the Mathlib stabilizerHom_apply (simp) and span_singleton_eq_bot. I did not trace every simp call in the long Lift and Weierstrass proofs. I cannot run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour. I found no rewrite loops or competing-rule problems in the file's own simp lemmas. The findings are about missing simp-normal-form lemmas that force fragile fallbacks and repeated ad-hoc simpa calls. How far these fallbacks reflect the P2M scoping or private-def machinery is uncertain.

findings.excerpt: first | exact hA | simpa using hA | simpa +zetaDelta using hA
findings.problem: After `rw [mem_center_iff, ← mem_nonunits_iff]` the goal is `((p : integralClosure ℤ _) : AlgebraicClosure ℚ) ∈ A.nonunits`. This should normalize to `(p : AlgebraicClosure ℚ) ∈ A.nonunits` through the standard cast lemma for the subring coercion. The proof does not rely on that rule. It tries three alternatives, including `simpa +zetaDelta`, which suggests the author could not tell which cast normal form the simp set produces. By contrast, natCast_mem_primeBelow (lines 148–154) closes the same kind of goal with explicit `map_natCast` rewrites. Because `A.center` is a private def with no simp-normal-form lemma for `((p : integralClosure ..) : _)`, this step depends on defeq or ambient simp behaviour.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the `first | ...` chain with one deterministic step. For example, add a small `@[simp]`-free helper or use `rw [mem_center_iff, ← mem_nonunits_iff]; simpa only [Subring.coe_natCast] using hA`. Alternatively, state the cast fact once as a lemma `((p : integralClosure ℤ (AlgebraicClosure ℚ)) : AlgebraicClosure ℚ) = p` and `rw` with it. The lemma names are not tested.
findings.benefit: The proof no longer silently depends on whichever simp-set/defeq path happens to succeed, so it is less likely to break when simp lemmas change, and the intended normal form of a natural-number cast under the coercion is explicit.

findings.excerpt: first | exact h | simpa only [Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom_apply, hφ] using h | simpa +zetaDelta only [Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom_apply, hφ] using h
findings.problem: `ht'` uses a three-way fallback of `exact`, `simpa only`, and `simpa +zetaDelta only` to apply the simp lemma `stabilizerHom_apply` plus the local `hφ`. The goal depends on `let`/`letI` bodies (φ, φ₀, actL…), so which branch works depends on whether simp unfolds those `let`s. `hφ : ∀ b, φ (Ideal.Quotient.mk 𝔔 b) = Ideal.Quotient.mk 𝔔 ((rsh g * σ₀) • b)` is stated about a local `let` definition, so it is not a reusable simp rule. The fallback chain shows the simp normal form was not controlled.
findings.proposed_change: Make the intended rewriting explicit. Either `rw [Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom_apply] at h; exact h.trans (hφ b)`, or a `calc` that turns `h` into `ht'` without a simp fallback. Alternatively, `obtain ⟨φ, hφ⟩ : ∃ φ, ∀ b, φ (mk b) = mk (σ • b)`, to avoid `let` unfolding altogether.
findings.benefit: Replaces a trial-and-error `first` combinator with one deterministic step. This removes the `+zetaDelta` dependence and makes the proof robust to changes in how `let` bodies are treated by simp.

findings.declaration: repeated `Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)} ≠ ⊥` side goals (span_natCast_isMaximal, card_inertia_primeBelow_eq_ramificationIdx, ramificationIdx_primeBelow_ne_zero, and others)
findings.problem: The same unnamed fact `Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)} ≠ ⊥` for prime `p` is proved by an identical `simpa [Ideal.span_singleton_eq_bot] using hp.ne_zero` at lines 159, 778, 795, 820 and 884. Each use needs a non-reducible simp call whose result depends on how simp normalizes `((p : ℕ) : ℤ) = 0`. The ℤ-ideal side, `Ideal.span {(p:ℤ)} ≠ ⊥`, has no canonical lemma or simp normal form. By contrast, the ℤ[𝓞 L]-side facts `hp0`, `hspan0`, `hmap0` are each derived separately in adicValuation_natCast_eq_exp_neg_ramificationIdx.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma next to `span_natCast_isMaximal`, e.g. `theorem span_natCast_ne_bot (hp : p.Prime) : Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)} ≠ ⊥ := by simpa [Ideal.span_singleton_eq_bot] using hp.ne_zero`. Then pass `(span_natCast_ne_bot hp)` at the five call sites. It can also be derived from `(span_natCast_isMaximal hp).ne_top`-style facts, or reuse `IsMaximal.ne_bot` if available. This lemma should not be `@[simp]` because it carries a hypothesis.
findings.benefit: Removes five copies of an assumption-dependent simp call and gives the side condition a single named, auditable form. If `Int.natCast_eq_zero`/`Ideal.span_singleton_eq_bot` simp behaviour changes, only one proof needs repair.
